paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. On that mountain, Jesus shows who He really is. His face changes and His clothes become radiantly white (Luke 9:29). Moses and Elijah appear in glory and talk with Him about His departure, which He was about to accomplish at Jerusalem (Luke 9:30-31). So the glory and the cross belong to the same Jesus, and He walks toward Jerusalem knowing exactly what is ahead.

Then there's Peter. He wants to put up three shelters, one for Jesus, one for Moses and one for Elijah, and the writer adds, "He did not know what he was saying" (Luke 9:33). Friend, I have been Peter. I've opened my mouth in a big moment and the words came out before the thinking did, and I'm LOUDLY not judging him. But look at what God does next. He doesn't leave the three of them guessing. A voice comes from the cloud: "This is My Son, whom I have chosen. Listen to Him!" (Luke 9:35).

That command is the whole point, baker. Moses and Elijah are gone, and only Jesus is left with them (Luke 9:36). When you're not sure what to say or what to do, God's answer is the same: listen to Jesus. So read what He says, let it settle in, and keep coming back for more. I think that's how a heart gets ready for the big day.
